text.p: The following are the main stories from Friday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG

- German President calls for courage to take the risk for the sake of freedom in Europe, but expresses understanding for the apprehensions of citizens of the EU who are afraid of ceding more power to Brussels and giving up their currencies.
- Lawyers do not think courts are overburdened with work at lawyers' conference in Frankfurt
- Resistance from construction unions to proposals in pay arbitration talks. 1.3 percent more agreed for western German workers and a smaller Christmas bonus
DASA and Lagardere plan the third largest space company in the world
- Germany catches up in genetic technology
HANDELSBLATT
- German construction talks concluded agreement with compromise
- Social Democrats can not agree on holding further tax reform talks with Chancellor Helmut Kohl's ruling coalition
- German President Roman Herzog says Europe is more than just a currency zone in speech as he receives Charlemagne prize for promoting European integration
- Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber welcomes plans for DASA and Lagadere alliance
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl no longer believes there will be change in trend on jobs market in 1997, he said at the end of his visit to New Zealand
- German delegation accompanying Kohl conclude big Siemens deal in New Zealand
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Fight for jobs in construction sector is relentless. Sides in pay talks agree on compromise deal
- German President Roman Herzog says Europe is more than a market, as he receives Charlemagne prize for promoting European integration
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl says change in job market trend will not change this year
- The Bundesbank declined to comment on rumours that Japan, the United States and German planned intervention on currency markets
- Postbank head Guenter Schneider resigns. Protest against row over plans to combine post office and Postbank branches
- Airbus posted 707 million marks profit in 1996
- Bank clients should check their bank statements
DIE WELT
- Construction workers could go on strike again. Acceptance of arbitration agreement is unsure. Wages are to go up by 1.3 percent
- German President Roman Herzog hailed as a "president of renewal" is given German top political award, Charlemagne prize for European integration
- Chancellor Helmut Kohl does not see a change in the trend on the jobs market in 1997
- Lawyers' association meeting criticises legislators
- New arms industry giant in Europe. DASA and France's Lagadere group agree to cooperate in space technology and defence
- Postbank boss Guneter Schneider resigns in protest at agreement between the post offices services company and Postbank to create joint branches
- Finance Minister Theo Waigel announces further budget cuts
